items.stem: Why does repeatedly reading offsetHeight then changing styles in a loop cause 'layout thrashing'?

options.text: Each read forces a synchronous layout after the previous write invalidated it
options.rationale: Correct: interleaving reads and writes forces repeated reflows.

options.text: It causes the garbage collector to run
options.rationale: Thrashing is about forced reflow, not GC.
Layout runs on the main thread, not the network.
The compositor is not disabled by reads.

items.explanation: Correct: interleaving reads and writes forces repeated reflows.

items.stem: In the event loop, when do microtasks (e.g. resolved promise callbacks) run relative to macrotasks?

options.text: All pending microtasks drain before the next macrotask runs
options.rationale: Correct: the microtask queue is emptied after each task before rendering/next task.

options.text: Only when the stack is never empty
options.rationale: They run when the stack empties.

options.text: Microtasks and macrotasks run in registration order together
options.rationale: They are separate queues with microtasks prioritised.

items.explanation: Correct: the microtask queue is emptied after each task before rendering/next task.

items.stem: Which changes typically avoid a full layout (reflow)? (Select TWO)

options.text: Animating transform and opacity, which the compositor can handle
options.rationale: Correct: these can be composited without layout.

options.text: Batching DOM reads together and writes together
